verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents its own MCP client support: configured MCP servers expose external tools to the agent, and the docs show adding a hosted workflow tool (Linear) over HTTP. It also imports existing MCP configs from Claude Code and Cursor. The evidence never names Jira, Slack, or Google Drive connectors, though, so reaching those tools depends on suitable third-party MCP servers. Missing for 10: documented Jira, Slack, or Google Drive integrations, first-party connectors or a catalog for workflow tools, and independent hands-on corroboration of workflow-tool connections.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect the agent to workflow tools like Jira, Slack, and Google Drive to extend its context

citations.quote: MCP servers expose external tools to Grok. Once configured, their tools are available alongside the built-in ones
grok mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp
Grok also loads MCP configurations from `~/.claude.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, and project `.mcp.json` files
